transcript_text:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Rajiv (VP Eng), Hannah (Security), Tom (CTO), Alicia (SRE)
---
Summary: short scoping call to align on pilot success criteria (latency and cost KPIs), workload sizing for benchmark, and security/compliance gating (SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS). Agreed next steps and owners.
Topics: success criteria, benchmark plan, data residency, SSO and RBAC mapping, audit log retention and format, timeline for pilot run.
Action items: see metadata list above.
---
0:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, im maya, your ae, and luis is our se who will run the bench and the private deployment checks.
0:22 Tom Suarez: hey thanks, Tom here. short on time so appreciate the succinct rundown.
0:30 Luis Ortega: hi all, quick agenda - confirm acceptance criteria, capture workload (qps/payload), security gates, and schedule bench window.
0:45 Rajiv Patel: perfect. for context, we are building an SMS routing assistant and will call the model for classification + routing + short generation. this will be mixed sync/async with strict p95 latency targets.
1:10 Hannah Lee: plus we have to meet corporate security: SOC 2 type 2, ISO 27001 is preferred, SSO via SAML, RBAC integration with our IdP groups, and audit logs shipped to our SIEM. data residency: EU for EU customers.
1:35 Luis Ortega: good to know. on the platform side Redwood offers hosted or Dedicated or a Private VPC deployment. for the pilot we recommend dedicated pool with private networking if you need EU residency and KMS integration.
2:05 Rajiv Patel: timeline — we want to run a 2-week pilot then decide by end of april. pilot success: under 150ms p95 for classification (short context), generation under 600ms p95 for the 128-token path, and cost per 1k requests to be within our projected budget.
2:40 Maya Chen: can you confirm acceptable SLOs and any hard cutoffs?
2:46 Rajiv Patel: hard cutoff is 800ms for any request; p95 goals as above. also need error budget: less than 1% 5xx of calls.
3:05 Alicia Gomez: on sizing - our current SMS burst is 200 rps sustained with 800 rps peaks during promos, average payload ~90 tokens, 95th token length ~180. we also expect lots of small classification calls that are 1-2 tokens.
3:35 Luis Ortega: that mix is helpful. for benching we'll emulate a split 70% classification (short tokens), 30% generation (longer tokens), and include KV-cache warm vs cold scenarios.
4:00 Hannah Lee: for compliance we need the following: SOC2 report, list of subservice providers, ISO cert copy if available, SSO/SAML metadata and SAML assertion encryption options, RBAC docs, audit log schema, and proof of encryption at rest with your KMS.
4:28 Maya Chen: we have a security pack - it includes SOC2 report, ISO binder (if requested), our SOC2 auditor name, and a KMS integration guide. i'll send a link to the secure share after the call.
4:45 Tom Suarez: important question — will audit logs include request/response hashes or redacted prompt text? we cannot send PII to external providers.
5:00 Luis Ortega: by default we capture request metadata, timestamps, model version, per-token cost, and a request id. payloads can be redacted; we offer configurable redaction and only store hashes if you prefer. also ship logs to your SIEM over syslog/forwarder or push to an s3 bucket in your VPC.
5:35 Hannah Lee: s3 in our VPC is preferable. retention requirement is 7 years for certain records, but for pilot we need at least 90 days. can your audit logs be exported in a normalized JSON schema?
6:00 Luis Ortega: yes we can. we will share the schema. note: retention beyond standard needs to be agreed in the private deployment contract.
6:20 Rajiv Patel: encryption — we use GCP KMS for keys in EU. can Redwood integrate with our KMS or do you use your own?
6:30 Maya Chen: for Private and Dedicated with VPC we can integrate customer-managed KMS via key wrapping or HSM. for hosted we use our KMS but offer bring-your-own-key for certain enterprise plans. we'll include integration details in the runbook.
6:55 Alicia Gomez: network wise, we cannot route traffic outside EU for EU tenant traffic. need proof that processing for EU data stays in EU region and that fallbacks won't route to US.
7:15 Luis Ortega: we support region pinning and can configure routing policies to ensure EU models stay in EU region; fallback policies are configurable and we can disable cross-region fallback for the pilot.
7:40 Hannah Lee: RBAC — we need role mapping to our IdP groups and SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning ideally. who owns user sync?
8:00 Maya Chen: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. our Console has role templates (admin, dev, auditor). we can map IdP groups to those roles and we support JIT provisioning.
8:20 Rajiv Patel: can we have an auditor-only role that sees logs but not full prompts?
8:28 Luis Ortega: yes, we can create restricted roles. logs can be exported to your SIEM without exposing raw prompts.
8:42 Tom Suarez: on the bench itself — what metrics will you provide during the run?
8:50 Luis Ortega: we'll provide p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, CPU/GPU utilization on nodes, token/sec, cost per 1k calls, error rates, and trace samples. we'll also run a cold KV-cache test and warm cache test to show delta.
9:15 Alicia Gomez: we need reproducible harness. will you share the test driver?
9:20 Luis Ortega: yes, we'll provide the test harness (k6-based or custom go load driver) and a script to replay sample traces. you'll run from our orchestrated runner or we can run in your VPC for the private deployment.
9:45 Hannah Lee: what about model version pinning and rollback? if we see quality regressions we need immediate rollback to previous model.
9:55 Maya Chen: platform supports model pinning and automatic fallback; during pilot we can pin to a stable tag and test canary in parallel. rollback is instant to prior version; we'll document the process.
10:12 Rajiv Patel: success criteria recap: p95 latency numbers, error budget under 1%, cost per projected 1M requests within 15% of forecast, RBAC + SAML working, logs delivered to our SIEM with retention policy met.
10:34 Maya Chen: yes, i'll add these as acceptance criteria in the runbook. any other legal or procurement gating?
10:45 Tom Suarez: procurement will want DPA + data residency addendum and subprocessors list. procurement timeline ~3 weeks after pilot greenlight.
11:00 Maya Chen: we'll provide a standard DPA and an addendum for residency.
11:10 Luis Ortega: bench logistics — propose we do an initial smoke bench on your dev data the week of 3/23, then two full runs (cold + warm) on 3/30 and 4/06, results consolidated the week of 4/07. does that align with your internal timeline to decide end of April?
11:35 Rajiv Patel: yes that fits. we'll aim for decision deadline 4/28.
11:45 Hannah Lee: one more technical — audit log fields: need request_id, timestamp, model_id, model_version, tenant_id, user_id (hashed), action, status_code, response_hash, redaction_flag. can you include those?
12:10 Luis Ortega: we'll map our fields; response_hash we can emit, and redaction_flag will note if payload was redacted.
12:25 Alicia Gomez: we'll also send sample traces and a list of peak windows.
12:35 Maya Chen: perfect. i'll share the security pack and runbook. action items and owners as discussed.
12:45 Tom Suarez: thanks all, appreciate the clear plan.
12:50 Rajiv Patel: thanks, speak soon.
---
Post-call notes:
- Redwood to mark pilot as Dedicated EU region with customer-managed KMS for pilot unless customer elects private on-prem.
- Bench schedule proposed and accepted; Luis to lead runs; Alicia to coordinate traffic traces.
- Security deliverables to be shared via secure share; procurement docs queued after pilot.
